Tesla's Cybercab program appears to be moving one step closer to reality. 

A steering-wheel-free Cybercab was recently spotted driving autonomously and smoothly parking itself at Tesla's factory, while more Robotaxis continue to accumulate around production areas.

Perhaps even more interesting, Cybercabs are now appearing alongside regular vehicle staging zones potentially signaling a shift toward larger-scale production.

The technology is impressive, but building and managing a massive autonomous fleet may be the real challenge ahead.

The Robotaxi era is getting closer. 🚀
©️@JoeTegtmeyer




Joe Tegtmeyer 🚀 🤠🛸😎 (@JoeTegtmeyer)

Cybercab production continues today & I think I captured an autonomously driving version without a steering wheel making a graceful arrival & then backing smoothly into a parking space on the W side of the EOL! 

We see many lined up outside the E of the main factory at the exit point with “Robotaxi” on the sides & the rear hatch & for the 1st time, Cybercabs are interspersed into the regular vehicle transportation staging areas, which itself may be a good indicator that production changes are underway.

Good to be back & seeing all the Cybercabs around the site!

I recently was at BVB, a company in Basel, Switzerland that had a lot of great inputs as to how building, managing & scaling a fleet service like @robotaxi & how this may be one of the biggest limiting factors to the speed of deployment that nobody (but me) is talking about.

I posted that video here on X yesterday, so check that out too for more context & thoughts on what we might be seeing with @Tesla.

TOSV is teaming up with @eightsleep for a casual Bay Area member meetup built around the kind of technology our community loves: smart, useful, and designed to make everyday life better.

​Join us on Saturday, June 20, for coffee, donuts, and a hands-on experience with Eight Sleep’s new House of Sleep mobile showroom.

​What to expect:

​- Coffee and donuts provided by TOSV
- A casual opportunity to connect with fellow Tesla owners and tech enthusiasts
- A private, hands-on demo inside Eight Sleep’s 16-foot glass-walled mobile showroom
